name: Natural Language Processing & LLMs
description: Citation network of foundational deep learning architectures and language models.

nodes.title: Attention Is All You Need
nodes.abstract: We propose the Transformer, a novel neural network architecture based solely on attention mechanisms, dispensing with recurrence and convolutions entirely. Experiments show superior translation quality while being more parallelizable.

nodes.title: BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers
nodes.abstract: We introduce BERT, designed to pre-train deep bidirectional representations from unlabeled text by conditioning on both left and right context in all layers. It achieves state-of-the-art results on eleven NLP tasks.

nodes.title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks
nodes.abstract: We explore RAG architectures combining parametric memory from pre-trained sequence-to-sequence models with non-parametric memory backed by dense vector indexes of Wikipedia for open-domain question answering.

nodes.title: Sentence-BERT: Sentence Embeddings using Siamese Networks
nodes.abstract: We present Sentence-BERT (SBERT), a modification of pretrained BERT using siamese and triplet network structures to derive semantically meaningful sentence embeddings comparable via cosine similarity.

nodes.title: Language Models are Few-Shot Learners (GPT-3)
nodes.abstract: We demonstrate that scaling language models greatly improves task-agnostic few-shot performance. GPT-3 achieves strong results on NLP benchmarks without fine-tuning, operating purely via in-context prompting.

nodes.title: Word2Vec: Efficient Estimation of Word Representations
nodes.abstract: We propose two novel model architectures for computing continuous vector representations of words from vast datasets. Skip-gram and Continuous Bag-of-Words capture high-quality syntactic and semantic word relationships.

nodes.title: Exploring the Limits of Transfer Learning with T5
nodes.abstract: We introduce a unified text-to-text framework treating every NLP task as a text-generation problem, systematically evaluating pre-training objectives, architectures, and scaling strategies across diverse benchmarks.

nodes.title: RoBERTa: A Robustly Optimized BERT Pretraining Approach
nodes.abstract: We present a replication study of BERT pre-training demonstrating that training the model longer, with larger batches, and removing the next-sentence prediction objective yields substantially improved downstream performance.
